paper.title: Bounds on Treatment Effects From Studies With Imperfect Compliance
paper.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

paper_reference.paper_question: 在不完全遵从的二元 IV 设置中，全体 ATE 不能点识别时，sharp 上下界是什么？
paper_reference.target: ATE = E[Y(1)-Y(0)] for the whole population, not LATE for compliers.
paper_reference.source_location: Balke & Pearl (1997), JASA 92(439):1171-1176; project literature card and abstract-level alignment.
paper_reference.formula: The paper constructs sharp bounds for the average treatment effect under binary imperfect compliance from the observed joint distribution of (Y,D,Z). This package does not reproduce the closed-form bounds or their proof.
conditions: Binary instrument Z, binary treatment D, binary outcome Y.
No point identification of ATE in general.
what_paper_supports: LATE and ATE are distinct targets.
ATE is generally only partially identified under imperfect compliance.
Sharp bounds can be constructed in the binary IV model.
what_paper_does_not_support: It does not mean the current software has an IV/ATE-bounds backend.
It does not justify replacing ATE with LATE.
It does not make the 200-person synthetic table the paper data.

missing_condition.reason: No IV/ATE-bounds backend; sample-only data also cannot be upgraded to a population.

changed_target.reason: LATE is also unavailable; the system must not reuse the ATE question's materials as a LATE answer.

actual_run.note: No IV business run was attempted because there is no IV reader/backend.

notes: Holdout candidate. Paper bounds are recorded as paper reference only; software status is UNSUPPORTED. This is not a proof of non-identification.
